paras: The warning notices to Black residents of Colorado, Texas, were notices placed on the town's Black churches in the spring of 1903 warning "the colored people" to leave. The episode is known only from a one-sentence news brief in a Waxahachie paper of 11 May 1903, which gave no author, date or outcome.

According to the brief, a notice had been "placed on negro churches at Colorado, Coy, Tex.," with the place name apparently garbled in printing. The notice warned "the colored people to leave," addressing the Black population of the town as a whole rather than any named person. The brief did not say who posted the notice, when it appeared, or whether any reason was given in it.
No report of departures, violence, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

The Waxahachie Daily Light ran the item without a headline or comment in its "Minor Matters" column, a list of short state and national dispatches. There it sat between a note on the deaths of two elderly Waco citizens and a report of a shooting on a railroad locomotive in Tennessee, given no more weight than either.
No other white paper and no Black paper was found carrying the story, so its scale and outcome are not known.
